propositions: Push-first semantics with five in-loop retry cycles followed by exactly one conditional terminal push must be owned by the core push_tickets_branch function, replacing workflow-local retry logic.

Strict delivery mode must be opt-in via keyword-only parameter, default false, raise catchable PushDeliveryError with stable reasons and detail, and translate to process failure only at the Python adapter boundary.

All pre-existing library, CLI, MCP, and store-write callers must retain best-effort behavior by omitting strict parameter or reaching core with strict=False, preserving legacy return dispositions while inheriting corrected retry budget.
Distinct stable failure reasons must classify policy rejections separately from transport failures, each carrying git detail and unpushed-commit count.
Strict delivery must not write ticket events, emit BRIDGE_ALERT, or call sys.exit; core raises catchable exception, private module adapter translates to stderr and nonzero exit code.

Complete caller-contract matrix covering event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, delete, compact, and claim operations must be verified with no strict opt-in and unchanged legacy behavior.
